text: @DHSgov Aug 28, 2026, as posted: On August 27, ICE arrested Milo Yiannopoulos, an illegal alien from the United Kingdom, at the Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport (MSY) in Kenner, Louisiana. Yiannopoulos legally entered the country on May 14, 2019, through New York City, New York. He chose to overstay his welcome in violation of our nation’s laws. Yiannopoulos was issued a final order of removal by an Immigration Judge on July 22, after failing to show up for his immigration hearing. He will remain in ICE custody pending removal. Being in detention is a choice. We encourage all illegal aliens to take control of their departure with the CBP Home App. The United States is offering illegal aliens $3,000 and a free flight to self-deport now. We encourage every person here illegally to take advantage of this offer and reserve the chance to come back to the U.S. the right legal way to live the American dream. If not, you will be arrested and deported without a chance to return.

text: @BillMelugin_ Mar 16, 2026, as posted: WATCH: Four weeks ago, a frustrated ICE agent in the sanctuary city of Boston contacted me, telling me a group of anti-ICE agitators had just blown their operation to arrest a Salvadoran fugitive who is wanted in his home country on an arrest warrant for child rape & had been living near a Boston elementary school. name: Mario David Coronado-Juarez
crime: As posted: Upon further investigation the driver of the vehicle was Mario David Coronado-Juarez and not the vehicle’s registered owner. Coronado-Juarez was an illegal alien from Guatemala who was previously removed by Border Patrol from the United States in 2021.
text: @DHSgov Sep 24, 2026, as posted: On September 20, ICE officers attempted a stop of a vehicle registered to a known criminal illegal alien with multiple alcohol related driving offenses who is also wanted in Guatemala for a drunk and disorderly charge, during a targeted enforcement operation in Grand Rapids, Michigan. As officers attempted the stop to confirm the identity of the driver, the driver of the vehicle fled at a high rate of speed. In the interest of public safety, ICE officers immediately discontinued the enforcement action. A short time later, officers saw smoke nearly half a mile from the attempted stop and discovered the vehicle had crashed into a tree and caught fire. Officers immediately attempted to render aid and extinguish the fire until the Grand Rapids Police Department and Fire Department arrived. The driver was pronounced dead at the scene by local officials. Officials also estimated that the suspect’s vehicle was traveling well over 100 miles per hour when the crash occurred. Upon further investigation the driver of the vehicle was Mario David Coronado-Juarez and not the vehicle’s registered owner. Coronado-Juarez was an illegal alien from Guatemala who was previously removed by Border Patrol from the United States in 2021. He re-entered the country, a felony, at an unknown date and location. Resisting officers and evading arrest is dangerous for our officers, illegal aliens, and the public.

text: @HSISanJuan Jul 6, 2026, as posted: HSI Arrests BVI National for Illegal Reentry and Child Sexual Exploitation Charge in St. Thomas Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) in St. Thomas, in coordination with other federal law enforcement partners arrested Bruce Wheatley, a citizen of the British Virgin Islands, for illegal reentry after removal and multiple federal child exploitation offenses. On June 26, 2026, Wheatley was apprehended in Havensight, St. Thomas, after identification by federal agents. Wheatley had previously been removed from the United States to the British Virgin Islands on May 9, 2026, after being ordered removed by an Immigration Judge. During the investigation, HSI agents discovered evidence of additional criminal activity. A review of Wheatley's phone revealed videos containing child sexual abuse material. The U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of the Virgin Islands has accepted prosecution for violations of Title 8 USC 1326 (Reentry of a Removed Alien), as well as Title 18 USC 2252 (Receipt, Distribution, and Possession of Visual Depictions of Sexually Explicit Conduct Involving a Minor). Yariel Ramos, Acting Special Agent in Charge of HSI San Juan said: “The arrest of Bruce Wheatley underscores the unwavering commitment of Homeland Security Investigations to protect our communities from individuals who repeatedly violate our nation's laws and exploit the most vulnerable among us. The discovery of child sexual abuse material is deeply disturbing and HSI will continue to work tirelessly with our partners to ensure that those who commit these heinous crimes are brought to justice. We are grateful for the swift and coordinated efforts of our agents and law enforcement partners in this case." HSI in St. Thomas continues to work with local authorities to pursue further investigative actions and coordinating with the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) to assist in victim identification. Report any suspicious activity by calling the HSI San Juan Communications Center at 787-729-6969. @ICEgov

text: @ICEgov Nov 23, 2026, as posted: TWICE-DEPORTED MS-13 GANG MEMBER ARRESTED BY ICE IN HOUSTON Samuel Jeremias Grande-Caminos, an illegal alien from El Salvador and documented MS-13 gang member, was arrested by @EROHouston during a targeted operation. Grande-Caminos was previously deported twice, convicted of felony illegal re-entry in 2016, and illegally entered the U.S. a THIRD time. After three weeks of surveillance, ICE’s Delta Team officers swiftly apprehended him in a pre-dawn operation. Cooperation between ICE and the Houston Police Department has been essential to getting dangerous criminals off our streets. Now, Houston Mayor John Whitmire’s new order undermines this critical partnership, putting public safety at risk and making it harder for ICE to get dangerous criminals off our streets. ICE will NOT be deterred. We will continue arresting dangerous criminals and keeping American communities safe.

name: Bruno Teixeira Badaia

crime: Charged: ICE transferred Rajinder Kumar, a criminal illegal alien from India, to Oregon state custody to face prosecution in connection with the deaths of two newlywed Americans. Kumar has been indicted in Deschutes County, Ore., on 2 counts of first-degree manslaughter.
text:
@ICEgov Oct 18, 2026, as posted: ICE transferred Rajinder Kumar, a criminal illegal alien from India, to Oregon state custody to face prosecution in connection with the deaths of two newlywed Americans. 

Kumar has been indicted in Deschutes County, Ore., on 2 counts of first-degree manslaughter and other related charges stemming from a deadly November 2025 tractor-trailer accident. 

After his local arrest, ICE lodged an immigration detainer with the Deschutes County Jail, but in April 2026, Deschutes County released Kumar from custody without honoring ICE’s detainer. ICE officers subsequently located and arrested Kumar at large earlier this year. 

Following the conclusion of state criminal proceedings, ICE will pursue Kumar’s immigration case consistent with federal law.
